The earlier OpenRouter finding is resolved, the production-path evidence supports the correction, and no remaining actionable defect was found. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `b254db6952bff42aa0148a6b6debaa841f5257ef` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused, well-supported fix with the prior compatibility defect corrected and no remaining blocking finding. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (terminal): Current-head loopback HTTP evidence exercises registered Qwen/OpenRouter providers through the real transport, failure owner, and profile writer/readers, showing model-scoped throttling and preserved billing controls. Earlier complete Qwen agentCommand traces additionally establish automatic provider loading and persisted session outcomes; they are historical, not a claimed current-head rerun. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (terminal): Current-head loopback HTTP evidence exercises registered Qwen/OpenRouter providers through the real transport, failure owner, and profile writer/readers, showing model-scoped throttling and preserved billing controls. Earlier complete Qwen agentCommand traces additionally establish automatic provider loading and persisted session outcomes; they are historical, not a claimed current-head rerun. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Introduced production change: The pinned merge-base-to-head change adds a Qwen classifier registered for Qwen, Qwen Token Plan, and legacy Bailian Token Plan. It requires HTTP 429 and recognized structured evidence before refining allocation errors.
Prior finding resolved: The GitHub commit patch confirms the correction restricts provider precedence to billing or rate_limit. Current tests cover OpenRouter’s generic timeout hook, nested upstream billing, and explicit key-budget billing without local profile-health writes.
Current main still needs the fix: Fetched main retains the generic HTTP 429 billing precedence and has no Qwen classification hook in its provider registrations. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Provider errors feed OpenClaw’s failover classifier, which determines retry and saved-profile health. The Qwen plugin supplies vendor-specific error meanings while shared recovery code applies cooldowns or billing disables. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Provider HTTP error] --> B[Transport preserves error details] B --> C[Qwen error classifier] C --> D[Shared HTTP classification] D --> E[Temporary limit] D --> F[Billing failure] E --> G[Model cooldown] F --> H[Profile disable] ``` ## Before merge None.

Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/148236 - Defines the exact provider response and incorrect profile-disable outcome. - `same_root_cause`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/148275 - Addresses the same report using a different classification boundary and remains unmerged. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep Qwen error semantics in its existing provider hook and reuse shared cooldown handling while preserving genuine billing and OpenRouter behavior. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, source establishes the failure path: a documented Qwen HTTP 429 insufficient_quota response reaches generic billing classification and profile disable. This read-only review did not execute a current-main reproduction. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. The patch uses the existing provider-owned classification hook and a narrow shared precedence correction, with controls for genuine billing and other providers. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant.
